$Comment: Enchanter Orrin, the character who hands out the Disenchanting Table quests and takes their deliveries: an Outlander priest who walked away from the cult and now draws the void back out of gear. A thin variant: Template_Mmo_QuestGiver (shipped in the MMO Skill Tree jar, a thin layer over ziggfreed-common's Template_Zig_QuestGiver) holds the entire body - the idle / watch / interact behaviour and the press-F action - and this file only says what makes Orrin look and read as Orrin. Point a placement's Identity.Role at "Mmo_Enchanter" to stand him somewhere; this pack does so in NpcPlacements/Mmo_Enchanter_Temple.json. Modify may name ONLY the parameters that template declares: Appearance, NameTranslationKey, Weapons, OffHand, DefaultOffHandSlot. Naming anything else makes the engine refuse the whole role, which shows up in game as a character who never appears. Appearance is a Model asset id, so any vanilla model works here; the priest's robes are what mark him as a man of the cult, so swapping the model changes who he reads as. Weapons is what he holds, first entry in hand; the purple grimoire is the book the table's own ritual puts in a worker's hands, so he reads as an enchanter at a glance. NameTranslationKey is his nameplate, shipped in this pack's npcs.lang. The press-F prompt is baked into Template_Zig_QuestGiver and shared with every giver using it; to give one its own prompt, copy Template_Zig_QuestGiver, edit the copy's Hint, and Reference the copy instead.
